subject: Biology
title: Active Transport
description: A quick, practical guide to Active Transport.

hook.text: Sometimes cells need to push molecules the wrong way—from low concentration to high.

buildup.text: Active transport uses ATP energy to pump molecules against their natural gradient.

discovery.text: The sodium-potassium pump moves 3 sodium ions out and 2 potassium ions in per ATP.

twist.text: Your brain spends about 70% of its energy just running these pumps in neurons.

climax.text: Without active transport, nerve signals, muscle contractions, and heartbeats all stop.

quiz.question: What does the sodium-potassium pump require to function?

details.summary: Active transport uses cellular energy in the form of ATP to move molecules against their concentration gradient, from areas of low concentration to high concentration. This is essential for maintaining the ion imbalances that power nerve signals and muscle contractions.
details.whyItMatters: Without active transport, cells could not maintain the chemical gradients needed for nerve impulses, nutrient absorption, or waste removal. It is the energy-consuming workhorse that keeps cells alive and functional.
takeaways: Active transport requires ATP energy to move molecules against gradients
The sodium-potassium pump maintains electrical potential across cell membranes
Active transport enables nutrient uptake and waste removal against gradients

faq.question: How does the sodium-potassium pump work?
faq.answer: It uses one ATP molecule to pump three sodium ions out and two potassium ions into the cell. This creates an electrical gradient across the membrane essential for nerve signaling, muscle contraction, and maintaining cell volume.

faq.question: What is the difference between active and passive transport?
faq.answer: Passive transport moves molecules down their concentration gradient without energy, like diffusion and osmosis. Active transport moves them against the gradient, requiring ATP energy. Cells use both to maintain the precise internal conditions needed for survival.
